batch: Gpg4win 5.1.1 installer scope and component-control source review

authenticode.signer: E=code@g10code.com, CN=g10 Code GmbH, O=g10 Code GmbH, L=Erkrath, S=Nordrhein-Westfalen, C=DE

sourceFindings: The outer NSIS installer configures the MultiUser command-line mode and comments that user-mode installation is supported, though system-wide installation is preferred.
The outer source exposes the component page and loads previously remembered choices before calculating dependencies.

The 5.1.1 component source reads `inst_kleopatra`, `inst_okular`, `inst_gpgpass`, `inst_gpgoljs`, `inst_gpgol`, `inst_gpgex`, `inst_paperkey` and `inst_browser` boolean values from an explicit configuration file path passed with `/C=<path>`.
`/MINIMAL=1` explicitly deselects Kleopatra and several other components, then selects Paperkey; it does not implement the user's GnuPG-plus-Kleopatra selection.
The nested GnuPG installer is required and is launched silently into a directory beside the Gpg4win installation.

The Gpg4win uninstaller checks GnuPG registrations in both registry views and invokes the registered nested GnuPG uninstallers. An unrelated pre-existing GnuPG registration must not be silently adopted or removed.
outcome: The confirmed user component choices are technically expressible through the explicit config file; package-specific config staging, current-user mode, nested dependency ownership, and removal/key-data preservation still require implementation and Windows acceptance. No installer or product was executed.
deferred: Verify outer and nested current-user scope in the disposable VM.
Add package-specific generation and cleanup of the component config file, with explicit true/false values for all optional integrations.
Detect and safely handle existing GnuPG/Gpg4win registrations before install or removal.
Verify `%APPDATA%/gnupg` and other user-owned key/configuration data survive install, repeat, remove and recovery.
Run package lifecycle and feature acceptance on supported disposable Windows targets.
